items.title: Jon Hendricks interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 29, 2000 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: They’ve listened to Orrin Hatch try to justify the fact that he is humane enough to run for president while citing the fact, that, “I have many Jewish friends — I have this 92-year old lady who is a Jewish lady, a very good friend of mine.”

ctx.x: Yeah sure. I think these things are important. I think what you’re doing is important. I think that younger students especially need to feel some contact with people they may never have seen in their lifetimes, but whom, if they’re studying jazz, have an impact on them. That’s the value of this. It’s like a volume of history, but it’s living history. These kinds of things are going to supercede history books. I don’t think there’ll be history books far into the future, especially if people write history as it…
Because everybody will know about it.
